provenance: Corrections to the imported OpenTyria tables in messages.json, from the two sources that can actually arbitrate: our own captures of client build 38797, and the client's own message-format tables recovered from Gw.exe (see studies/msgtable/FINDINGS.md). Kept beside messages.json rather than inside it so that regenerating the imported catalog cannot silently revert a verdict the client already gave us. Applying every entry here leaves zero residual disagreement between our catalog and build 38797's tables. NOTE ON RISK: the codec reads only `fields`; `declared_unpack_size`, `variable_length` and msg_header `length` are metadata it never consults. Of these entries, only GAME_SMSG 140, 146 and 421 change a field list, and Rurik sends none of those three -- so adopting this file changed no behaviour. Its value is that the catalog stops disagreeing with the binary, so later work is not built on a wrong flag. ADDED 2026-08-10: seven GAME_CMSG entries carrying `name` and the evidence for it, from two labelled input runs (toolkit/authsrv/labelrun.py, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md). The catalog had field layouts for 194 GAME_CMSG opcodes and names for NONE of them. These change NO field list -- the layouts are copied verbatim from messages.json and already agree with the client's own tables -- so they cannot affect decoding; they record what a message MEANS, which the binary's marshalling types cannot say. In particular 0x0040's u32 typing is correct and was nearly 'fixed' to float: the values are floats, the wire type is not, and the client's own SEND table says u32. ALSO 2026-08-10, later the same day: 0x0040 MOVE_UNKNOWN_FLOATS became ROTATE_PLAYER. That one was settled by the BINARY rather than by a labelled run -- the client's own assertion text names the quantity `rotation` -- and it is worth noting why the labelled runs could not have got there. A labelled run shows you WHEN a message is sent; it cannot show you that an infinity is a sentinel constant loaded from .rdata, and it was the infinities that made an angle look impossible. The wire evidence had been sitting in the vault since 2026-08-04 saying otherwise (every finite value inside +/-pi) and nobody had counted more than twelve of them. ADDED 2026-08-10 (second pass): twenty GAME_SMSG entries carrying `name`, `name_confidence` and the evidence, from a 30-opcode naming pass over the four live tapes of capture 20260807T143055 (10,944 real ArenaNet GAME_SMSG messages, 146 distinct opcodes, framing 100% clean) joined to the client's own dispatch handlers and its 19,620 compiled assert sites. Before this file had ONE named GAME_SMSG opcode of 487; it now has 21. Every entry changes NO field list -- the layouts are copied verbatim from messages.json and already agree with the client's own tables -- so none of them can affect decoding; they record what a message MEANS. `name_confidence` is the POST-REFUTATION value: each proposal was re-derived by a second reader told to refute it, which struck four headline citations and two verdicts. Ten further opcodes came back PARTIAL and are deliberately NOT named here; see studies/smsg/FINDINGS.md for those and for what was killed.

38.name: ATTACK
38.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C4 and C9. The operator was prompted to attack a targeted hostile and the client sent this with that agent's id, immediately after 0x00C1 selected it. It is ATTACK and not a general interact: prompted to TALK TO a friendly NPC the same client sent 0x0039 instead, and clicking a player sent neither. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl step `attack`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl steps `target_npc`/`interact_npc`/`target_player`.

57.name: INTERACT
57.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C9. Sent when the operator clicked and then talked to a friendly NPC -- once with the select, three more on repeated interaction, always carrying that NPC's agent id. Clicking a PLAYER produced target-select alone and no 0x0039, so this is about interactable agents rather than about clicking. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl steps `target_npc` and `interact_npc` (agent 45).

61.name: MOVE_SET_HEADING
61.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C5. Field 3 (the second vec2) is a DIRECTION, not a position: across 8 samples in a session where the character COULD NOT MOVE -- so field 1 never changed -- its magnitude held at 766.8 +/- 0.4% while its angle swept the compass. A fixed-length rotating vector is a heading. This corroborates OpenTyria's TURN_TO_DIRECTION from a property the schema itself does not state. Field 4 is a small integer 1..8 whose meaning is UNVERIFIED -- it looked like an eight-way compass across 11 consecutive samples in one window and collapsed across all 26 (value 1 spans 0.0-359.1 deg), so it is NOT the absolute heading. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl.

64.name: ROTATE_PLAYER
64.why: OBSERVED, from build 38797's own binary. Field 1 is an ANGLE IN RADIANS and field 2 is a normalised turn amount in (0,1]. Both are marshalled as u32 -- which is what the client's own SEND table says ([u32,u32], wire 10 bytes), so the typing here is CORRECT and must not be 'fixed' to float -- while their VALUES are IEEE-754 float32. THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS. (1) The client names the quantity itself: the public entry 0x008165C0 range-checks its float argument against the assert text `(rotation >= -1.0f) && (rotation <= 1.0f)` from P:\Code\Gw\Char\Cli\ChCliApi.cpp line 5562, then tail-calls the sender; that argument becomes field 2 (as its absolute value) and decides field 1's sign. There is exactly ONE site in the image that sends 0x0040 -- the 12-byte wrapper at 0x009207B0, found by enumerating all 174 callers of the channel send 0x007DCF00 and recovering the opcode immediate at each. (2) The +/-inf in field 1 is a literal SENTINEL, not a computed ratio: the sender loads +inf from .rdata 0x00948654 when rotation > 0 and -inf from 0x0094E538 when rotation < 0, and when rotation is exactly 0 sends atan2(current facing) with field 2 = 1.0. So an infinity means 'turning continuously, sign gives the direction' -- it does NOT rule out an angle, which is the inference that kept this opcode unnamed. (3) The wire agrees: of 559 samples across 55 game-channel streams, field 1 is never NaN and every one of the 163 finite values lies inside +/-pi (max 3.0190), and 16 of 162 equal atan2(dir.y,dir.x) of a nearby 0x003D direction vector to float32 round-off, 33 within 0.05 rad, against a null model whose 95th percentile is 5. WHICH SIGN IS A LEFT TURN IS UNVERIFIED (121/189 and 106/169 -- real but weak); no left/right claim is made here. CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN EARLIER TEXT: 'field 2 is exactly 1.0 in all 12 observed samples' was true of those twelve and false as a generalisation -- it is 1.0 in 433 of 559, with 105 at 0.425 and a tail down to 0.10133, which CORROBORATES studies/divergence/FINDINGS.md R3 (411/536 and 105 before the 2026-08-10 runs existed) rather than refuting it. The floor is the client's own send gate: it refuses to send below 0.1, and the observed minimum is 0.10133. CORPUS CAVEAT: 536 of the 559 are the harness clicking fixed window fractions, 22 are 2026-08-10 loopback (17 of them tape-loaded), and 1 is live -- so the FREQUENCIES describe our own driver, not a player. The name does not rest on them; it rests on the binary. UPSTREAM ldufr/Headquarter numbers ROTATE_PLAYER 0x0040 independently (GWCA has 0x003E, the known +2 drift); see PLAN.md 6.1 for its register row. Evidence: vault/captures/live/20260807T143055 conn :60935 msg 52 (field1 = 1.08214450 rad = 62.0026 deg, exactly atan2 of the (360.53,678.12) direction the three preceding 0x003D carry), and toolkit/authsrv/test_rotate.py, which re-measures the wire-side invariants every run.

70.name: USE_SKILL
70.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C1. Field 1 is the SKILL ID, not the skillbar slot, and field 3 is the target's agent id. THREE witnesses: the operator named the two skills they cast before any payload was decoded; the client's own skill and string tables resolve 153 and 105 to 'Vampiric Gaze' and 'Deathly Swarm'; and the tape's own 0x00DA SKILLBAR_UPDATE declared the bar as [153, 105, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. Pressing slots 1 and 2 sent 153 and 105 -- a slot index would have sent 0 and 1 -- and pressing the EMPTY slot 8 sent nothing at all, so the client validates occupancy locally. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl steps `skill_1`, `skill_2`, `skill_8`.

100.name: CHAT_SEND
100.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C2 and C10. Field 2 carries the typed text VERBATIM, including the channel prefix the CLIENT adds itself: typing `rurik one` sends `!rurik one`. EMOTES GO THROUGH THIS SAME MESSAGE as literal text (`/dance`, `/sit`, `/me waves`), so they are not a separate wire message and /sit is not distinguished from /dance in shape. Field 1 is the current target's agent id for slash commands and 0 for plain chat -- 6 samples across two sessions, two maps and three target allegiances, no counterexample. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl `chat_say`/`emote_dance`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl `emote_sit`/`emote_dance`/`chat_all`/`chat_me`.

193.name: TARGET_SELECT
193.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C3, CORROBORATED across three allegiances. Field 1 is the agent to select and 0 CLEARS the selection. Three Tab presses cycled 276 -> 273 -> 274; clearing sent 0; and it preceded every USE_SKILL, every ATTACK and every INTERACT with the matching id. Seen for a hostile, a friendly NPC and another player with no difference, so it is target-select and nothing more. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl `target_tab`/`target_clear`/`attack`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl `target_npc`/`target_player`.

140.why: Our table stops one field short. Binary cmds[] @VA 0x00bfff98 (file offset 0x7fef98) is [0x0000008c, 0x00000404, 0x00000404, 0x00000104]; the MsgFormatRecv entry @VA 0x00bc93a0 (file 0x7c83a0) statically holds count=4, i.e. cmds[0]+3 fields, and the next cmds[] array begins exactly 4 dwords later, so there is no room for more or fewer. Slots 1..3 are zero in the file and are written by the MSVC dynamic initializer at VA 0x00464650-0x0046466e (`a1 74 f8 bf 00 / a3 9c ff bf 00` etc.), copying the statically-present constants [0x00bff874]=0x404, [0x00bff878]=0x404, [0x00bff87c]=0x104. cmd 0x104 = type 4, count 1 = a 1-byte unsigned int (our `byte`). We are missing that trailing byte, so we frame this message as 10 bytes when the client writes 11 and every later message in the datagram shifts.

Initializer at VA 0x004661d0-0x00466216 copies the statically-present constants [0x00c015a8]=0x1805, [0x00c015ac]=0x404, [0x00c01668]=0x104, [0x00c015dc]=0x204, [0x00c015e4]=0x104, [0x00c01520]=0x404, [0x00c0152c]=0x104. The final 0x104 = type 4, count 1 = a trailing `byte` we do not have: 39 bytes, not 38. No type 7/11/12 field is present, so the message is FIXED, not variable_length.NAMED 2026-08-10, and it is the FIRST name any GAME_SMSG opcode has carried -- the imported catalog has field layouts for 487 of them and names for none. This one is earned the same way the seven GAME_CMSG names were: from a witness that was not consulted to make the claim. It is the GAME-channel twin of AUTH_SMSG 0x0009 GAME_SERVER_INFO. Field 1 is a sockaddr_in for the next instance (family u16 LE, port u16 BE, IPv4 -- the mixed endianness is the client's, and reading the port the other way round is a documented past failure), and fields 2, 4 and 6 are the next instance's world_id, map_id and player_id. EVIDENCE: across the three transitions in one recorded session, every one of those four values equals what the NEXT connection then sent in its own client-to-server VERSION frame -- 12 of 12 fields, parsed straight off wire.jsonl, which the decrypted channel files do not even carry. toolkit/authsrv/tape.py's chain() re-derives that every run and REFUSES a link it cannot prove, rather than ordering hops by timestamp. THE VALUES THEMSELVES ARE NOT RECORDED HERE and must not be: world_id and player_id are live session identifiers from the owner's own account, schema/ is tracked and the vault is not. Field 5 (offset +33) was 1, 0, 1 across the three hops, correlating with destination map 146/164/146 -- possibly an is-explorable flag, UNVERIFIED at n=3 with two of the three being the same map, so it stays unnamed. The 39-byte length this entry corrects is now CORROBORATED by ArenaNet's own stream as well as by the client's tables: in all three tapes the next message begins exactly 39 bytes later.

12.name: CLIENT_PERF_REQUEST
12.why: OBSERVED -- named for what the handler DOES, since the message carries nothing but its header. Its entire body: query GrPerf(counter=4, period=3) under GrPerf.cpp:291/292 'counter < GR_COUNTERS' and 'period < GR_PERIODS', derive a rate, read a global, and send 3 dwords back through MsgConn.cpp:1186. That send computes its wire opcode as '((conn+0x54) ? 0x8000 : 0) | msg[0]' -- which is where studies/divergence D4's mysterious client reply '0x8009' comes from. 79 in the corpus, exactly equal to 0x000D's 79, per connection. PING/KEEPALIVE is not refuted and is recorded as the live rival.

13.name: LATENCY_REPORT
13.why: OBSERVED. The store at 0x0048DA40 discards the value unless it is <= 5000 ('cmp esi,0x1388 / ja'), then memmoves a 36-byte ring and writes the newest sample at its head; the accessor walks up to 10 non-zero samples and returns (latest, mean). A current-and-average pair over a 10-deep ring is a latency graph and little else, and the UiRoot.cpp assert string 's_netGraph' sits immediately before one of that accessor's only two callers. 79 messages, exactly equal to 0x000C's 79 per connection (10/10, 29/29, 2/2, 3/3, 37/37).

30.name: WORLD_SIMULATION_TICK
30.why: OBSERVED. The single largest opcode in the live corpus (3971 of 10944, 36.3%) and it is a clock, not a heartbeat. The client names the one payload dword twice: 'message.time' where it arrives (AgMsg.cpp:208, VA 0x005fcf8b) and 'elapsedMs' where it is consumed (AgTimer.cpp:32, VA 0x00603ff2), and 0x00603fe0 walks a world-scoped timer queue firing everything now due. The wire then agrees on a check it could have failed: summing field 1 across a tape reconstructs that tape's own wall clock, first tick to last, at -1.2 ms over 48 s, -1.5 ms over 147 s, +18 ms over 13 s and +10 ms over 185 s. 445 distinct deltas, 1..520 ms. Rival rejected: HEARTBEAT/PING, which 36% of a corpus invites -- refuted because the payload is CONSUMED to drive a timer queue, not echoed or ignored.

32.name: WORLD_CREATE_AGENT
32.why: OBSERVED. The handler ALLOCATES rather than looks up -- 'mov ecx,0x134; call 0x0047F490' with AgMsg.cpp and line 270 in the operand registers, building a fresh 308-byte object, then asserts AgMsg.cpp:295 'ptr->IsInWorld()' on it. agint.h:929 bounds-checks fields 5/7 as a world position ('pos.x >= worldDims.x0' and its three siblings). AgAgent.cpp:180 'agentDef < arrsize(context->def)' puts field 3 into the class factory, and the client's own enum names its values: ChCliApi.cpp:4047 GW_AGENTDEF_CHAR, GdCliApi.cpp:430 GW_AGENTDEF_GADGET, ItCliApi.cpp:614 GW_AGENTDEF_ITEM. The body runs twice with the array base advanced 0x64, which AgAgent.cpp:312 names as m_world 0 and 1. 527 on the wire. Rival rejected: a state refresh, which has no allocation site and would resolve an existing pointer; this handler never does. Supersedes the OpenTyria name, which was UPSTREAM.

33.name: WORLD_REMOVE_AGENT
33.why: OBSERVED. AgMsg.cpp:316 'ptr' requires the slot named by field 1 to be non-null -- the agent must ALREADY exist, which is the create's mirror image. AgAgent.cpp:804 '(*curr)->m_bindTarget == this' sits in the per-world routine the handler calls, which walks every object bound to the agent. Same twice-with-base-advanced-0x64 world pair as 0x0020. On the wire: 416 messages, 416/416 naming an id 0x0020 created earlier in the same tape, 0 naming a never-created id and 0 double-removing without an intervening create -- an all-or-nothing check across the whole corpus.

37.name: AGENT_MOVE_DIRECTION
37.why: OBSERVED, and the discriminator against 0x0029 is the cleanest structural fact in the corpus: this message's vec2 is UNIT LENGTH in 201 of 201 samples (|v| in [0.99655, 1.00000]) while 0x0029's is 1119..21551 world units in 0 of 987. A direction and a destination, not two of the same thing. AgMsg.cpp:412 'syncPtr' and :418 'asyncPtr' show it applied twice, to the authoritative agent and the client's predicted copy. CONFIDENCE IS MEDIUM ON PURPOSE: no assert in this handler names field 1 or field 2; the byte's name comes from the sibling setter 0x002B uses (AgAgent.cpp:2368 '!(facing & ~AGENT_FACING_MASK)'), not from here.

38.name: AGENT_UPDATE_FLAGS
38.why: OBSERVED. AgAgent.cpp:2301 'm_flags & INTERNAL_FLAG_IN_WORLD' is asserted on entry to the setter the handler calls with field 2, and it tests dword [agent+0x20] -- naming that offset as m_flags. The setter's write is ((old ^ new) & 0x3f0000) ^ new: it KEEPS the old bits inside mask 0x3f0000 and takes the new bits everywhere else, so a server cannot set anything in that mask through this message. AgMsg.cpp:438/443 'syncPtr'/'asyncPtr' put it on the same two agent arrays as 0x0020 and 0x0021. 155 on the wire, 155/155 naming an agent created earlier in the same tape, 151 of them immediately after 0x006D as the create burst's tail.

41.name: AGENT_MOVE_TO_POINT
41.why: OBSERVED, and this CORROBORATES a name the server already shipped as a RECONSTRUCTION rather than resting on it. agint.h:929's four worldDims asserts are applied to field 2 before anything else happens, which settles position over direction -- the exact confusion that makes a rival plausible. AgMsg.cpp:513 'ptr' bounds-checks field 1 against the agent array; the handler builds {x,y,plane,0} and hands it to setter 0x00602a40, which writes the point into the agent's goal slots. 987 on the wire, none unit-length. Rival named and rejected: 0x002A, whose handler calls the SAME setter and differs by one push -- 0x0029 hardcodes 0 where 0x002A supplies a fifth wire field.

43.name: AGENT_UPDATE_SPEED
43.why: OBSERVED. The client asserts its own bounds on the float the handler pushes from field 2: AgAgent.cpp:2366 'moveSpeed >= AGENT_MIN_MOVE_SPEED' and :2367 'moveSpeed <= AGENT_MAX_MOVE_SPEED', and :2368 '!(facing & ~AGENT_FACING_MASK)' on the byte from field 3. 163 wire samples land inside those bounds 163/163 (0.2778..1.0000) -- a check the corpus could have failed. 7 of the 15 distinct speeds are exact multiples of 1/288, which is Guild Wars' documented player run speed. REFUTES the server's own 'SpeedModifier / modifier, type' gloss: the field is CAPPED at 1.0, so no buff can ride it, and the third field is facing, not a type.

46.name: AGENT_UPDATE_ROTATION
46.why: OBSERVED, and it REFUTES the upstream rotation_cos/rotation_sin reading outright: sin^2+cos^2 over the corpus ranges 1.23..4.87 and is never 1. Field 2 is an absolute angle -- 55 finite values, ALL inside [-pi, pi], and the only non-finite values are exactly +inf (4) and -inf (5), the same two .rdata sentinels that named GAME_CMSG 0x0040. Field 3 is a turn rate in rad/s with exactly three distinct values (0.24892, 0.89012, 2.0943952 = 14.26, 51.00, 120.00 deg/s; the last is 2*pi/3 to the bit), per-agent constant in 29 of 31 agents. AgMsg.cpp:629/635 syncPtr/asyncPtr, setter 0x00602cc0 asserting AgAgent.cpp:2438. Keep both fields typed dword -- the values are floats, the marshalling is not, exactly as for ROTATE_PLAYER.

72.name: AGENT_SET_TABARD_VISIBLE
72.why: INFERRED from the call it gates, not from an assert naming the bit -- hence medium. The flag gates 0x0082dbb0, whose arguments the client asserts as CpsApi:520 'composite', CpsApi:504 'teamColorId' and :505 'composite', and CpsTex:459 pairs 'teamColorId || tabard'. On the wire: 130 messages over 58 agents, field 2 only ever 0 or 1, no agent ever receiving both; the agent set is EXACTLY 0x006E's (58/58) and it immediately follows 0x006E 130/130 times.

86.name: NPC_UPDATE_PROPERTIES
86.why: OBSERVED, and it closes to the exact byte, which is the check this repo prefers over one our own decoder forces true: the handler memsets a 0x20-byte local and fills it from wire fields 2..8, but the record has a HOLE at +0x18 -- so the seventh wire field lands LAST, not seventh, and a server packing seven fields contiguously puts it one slot early. Field 1 is a raw array index (the worker grows the array to index+1 and asserts 'index < m_count'), so it is a definition slot, not a handle. ChCliApi.cpp:6312 'baseClass == CHAR_CLASS_MONSTER_BASE' names the id space. 62 on the wire, 50 of them immediately followed by 0x0057.

87.name: MONSTER_COMPOSITE
87.why: SOURCED, from an assert inside this very handler: CharMsg.cpp:4438 'message.compositeCount <= MONSTER_COMPOSITE_MAX_DWORDS' at VA 0x0091de1f, guarding field 2's element count before the rep movsd that copies it. The client's own word for the message, in the message's own handler. On the wire: 50 messages, every one immediately preceded by an 0x0056, field 1 matching that 0x0056's field 1 in 50/50 with 0 orphans; element counts 1 and 2, both under the asserted bound of 8.

89.name: PLAYER_INFO
89.why: OBSERVED. CharData:178 'slot < arrsize(s_appearanceSlot)' and :180 'data.slot == slot' are hit with slot=3 and field 3 as the packed value, so field 3 is an appearance slot payload; ChCliApi:4966 '!(playerId & CHAR_CLASS_BASE_MASK)' names field 1's id space, and the function indexes the same 80-byte-stride array the name-plate module addresses by playerId. 61 on the wire; field 1 shares an id space with 0x00B0/0x00B1 field 1, and field 2 was created by an 0x0020 in the same tape 58/61.

110.name: AGENT_UPDATE_VISUAL_EQUIPMENT
110.why: SOURCED. ChCliApi.cpp:51 'No valid case for switch variable \'prop\'' IS the default arm of this worker's own 9-way jump table ('cmp ebx,8 / ja / jmp [ebx*4+0x8110c4]'), and the payload is exactly 9 dwords after the agent id -- the wire shape and the jump table agree without either producing the other. Two arms name themselves: ConstCostume.cpp:1188 'set - 1 < COSTUME_BODY_COUNT' on the prop-7 arm and :1217 'set - 1 < COSTUME_HAT_COUNT' on prop-8. 130 messages, 55 agents, followed by 0x0048 130/130. PRECONDITION for a server: every id here must have been declared by a prior 0x015E/0x0161 (621/621 on ArenaNet's own traffic).

166.name: AGENT_SET_PROFESSION
166.why: OBSERVED. GmDeckBuilder:2321 'agentPrimaryProf != agentSecondaryProf' gives the client's own name for the pair AND its own invariant; AcctTemplate:411/412 bound both against CHAR_PROFESSIONS. The wire obeys the invariant it was not told about: 136 messages, field 2 in 1..6 with value 0 NEVER occurring, field 3 in 0..8 with 0 as the mode -- a primary that must exist and a secondary that need not.

177.name: PLAYER_SET_PARTY
177.why: INFERRED -- the mechanism is exact but the noun 'party' is our reading, hence medium. ChCliApi:4966 '!(playerId & CHAR_CLASS_BASE_MASK)' is asserted on the register that three instructions later indexes the array this handler writes; PtUtil:221 'leader' is the party module's word for the role field 2 points at. 162 on the wire: field 1 is a playerId the same tape created via 0x0059 in 161/162 and field 2 in 150/162, NEVER a value the tape did not create. TRAP: the subject link runs from 0x00B0's field 1 to this message's SECOND word, so the pair reads [new, old] -- an assumption that both are the same field gets it backwards.

240.name: AGENT_INITIAL_STATUS
240.why: OBSERVED, and it renames rather than discovers: our server called this AGENT_INITIAL_EFFECTS from a RECONSTRUCTION, and the client's word is m_status, not effects. ChCliInt.h:254 'IS_TRUE(m_status & CHAR_STATUS_DEAD)' compiles to 'test byte ptr [edi+0x10c], 0x10' -- that assert names the field the payload lands in. The effect subsystem is never reached. The 'effects' noun is traceable to OpenTyria's struct having a 'uint32 effects' member: one witness, and not the client. INITIAL vs UPDATE is settled by an asymmetry the wire could have refused: this message precedes its agent's own 0x0020 create 187/472 times and is the message IMMEDIATELY before it every time; 0x00F1 does this 0 times in 312. Filtering out 0x001E ticks, 472/472 of these are followed by their own create -- it is a create PREFIX.

241.name: AGENT_UPDATE_STATUS
241.why: OBSERVED. Same field and same bit as 0x00F0 (ChCliInt.h:254), reached through the sibling setter AvApi.cpp:1423 twelve source lines after 0x00F0's at :1411. 0 of 312 arrive before their agent's create, against 0x00F0's 187 -- narrow and deep (34 distinct agents, one of them 42 times) where 0x00F0 is broad and shallow (187 agents, mostly once). Carries the burrow cycle's two 2.00 s windows: payload 0x0000 at 2.00 +/-0.06 s after create (148/148) and 0x1000 at 2.00 +/-0.06 s before remove (141/141), both exclusively for one creature class. REFUTES gw-preservation's INSTANCE_LOADED reading -- the handler takes an agent id and indexes a per-agent array.

319.name: ITEM_CREATE_BAG
319.why: OBSERVED. ItCliInv:38 'No valid case for switch variable \'bagType\'' is the client's own name for field 2; ItCliApi:1942 'inventory' guards the hash lookup keyed by field 1; ItCliBag:167 'slot != m_bagArray.Count()' is the remove-then-insert path keyed on field 4. Exactly 9 per tape in all four tapes, and the nine (bagType, field 3, capacity) triples are identical across all four: (1,0,20), (2,21,9), (3,6,12), (4,7..11,25) five times, (5,5,42). NOT a shippable constant table -- fields 1 and 4 are session-scoped ids a server must allocate itself.
